report.source_text: Two months after the initial presentation, the patient showed further ocular improvement. Visual acuity was stable, and fundus examination of both eyes revealed few cells in the lower vitreous cavity with unremarkable discs and dry macula (Fig. 2A). OCT of both eyes revealed prominent improvement with preserved contours and fewer retinal hyperreflective foci with preserved photoreceptor layers (Fig. 2B). He was advised to discontinue prednisone with further follow-up in our ophthalmology clinic.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 24-year-old male soldier presented with bilateral retinochoroiditis and vitritis following a 2-week prodrome of high fever (39°C), headaches, night sweats, transient generalized rash, and significant weight loss (10 kg in 10 days). Ophthalmic examination revealed bilateral macular retinitis with optic disc involvement. Systemic laboratory studies showed thrombocytosis, elevated atypical lymphocytes, elevated liver enzymes, and elevated ESR (24 mm/hr). Infectious workup excluded toxoplasmosis and syphilis. Serological testing confirmed positive Rickettsia typhi serology. The patient was treated with doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for four weeks and prednisone 50 mg daily. Three weeks after initiation of therapy, visual acuity improved to 20/20 bilaterally with resolution of active retinal inflammation, though mild residual vitritis and hypopigmented macular foci remained. At two-month follow-up, further ocular improvement was documented with OCT showing preserved photoreceptor layers and prednisone was discontinued.
